steps.title: Identify the population and the sample

skill.title: Find quartiles and the interquartile range
needs: Find mean, median and mode (incl. frequency tables)

note: Use the SAME method as the references (they are the lesson so far); change one thing, as usual. The method: Splits ranked data into halves, takes medians for Q1 and Q3, and subtracts for the IQR. Earlier backups were dropped for doing this instead: Solves a box-plot puzzle from a mix of summary statistics rather than finding quartiles/IQR from a list.

steps.title: Split the 12 ranked values into a lower and upper half

lines.text: There are 12 values, so the lower half is the first 6: $42, 64, 93, 94, 114, 114$.

steps.title: Find Q1 as the median of the lower half

lines.text: The median of 6 values is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: $93$ and $94$.

steps.title: Subtract to get the interquartile range
Write the median using the middle two values

lines.text: There are 12 ages, so the median is the mean of the 6th and 7th values. These are $x$ and $18$.

steps.title: Set the median equal to 17.5 and solve
Find Q3 from the top six ages

lines.text: With $x = 17$ the top six ages are $18, 18, 19, 22, 25, 30$. $Q_3$ is the median of these, the mean of the 3rd and 4th.
